verdicts.title: AGENTS.md points @requires_hf_auth at a helper file deleted in the same commit
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced every link. AGENTS.md:241-243 still reads 'Gated HuggingFace models use `@requires_hf_auth` imported from `packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/_helpers.py`'. `ls` on that path returns ENOENT; the file was deleted by 4b13d82a (PR #759, closing issue #538, which is itself already closed as completed). The mark now lives at /home/user/opaque/tests/_support/opaque_test_support.py:136-139 (`requires_hf_auth = pytest.mark.skipif(not has_hf_token(), ...)`), and every one of the ~30 import sites across packages/opaque-patches/tests and packages/opaque-transformers/tests uses `from opaque_test_support import requires_hf_auth`. The bare-module import only resolves because /home/user/opaque/conftest.py:13-21 inserts tests/_support onto sys.path and PYTHONPATH, so the correct incantation is genuinely non-obvious from the tree alone -- which is exactly why the AGENTS.md line matters. Not a duplicate: #538 is closed as completed by the same PR, so this is an uncorrected loose end from that merge, not tracked work. Severity stays low: it is a stale path in an agent-facing briefing file, no runtime or privacy impact, and the failure mode is a loud ImportError at collection rather than silent breakage.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A contributor or agent adds a gated-model test by following AGENTS.md:241-242 and writes an import against packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/_helpers.py, which no longer exists. Collection fails with ImportError. Because the working import (`from opaque_test_support import requires_hf_auth`) depends on the repo-root conftest.py injecting tests/_support onto sys.path -- not on any path visible from the test file -- the likely recovery is to hand-roll a local skipif copy of the mark, re-fragmenting the helper that PR #759 had just consolidated.

verdicts.title: Test comment asserts a PLD cross-test cache-contamination hazard that the current cache implementation does not have
verdicts.reasoning: Read both sides myself. packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py:414-418 carries the comment claiming the lru_cache 'keys on (process, kwargs), not the resolved global config'. That is false at 4b13d82: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_pld_cache.py declares `_CacheKey = tuple[DiscretizationConfig, Hashable, int | None]` (line 21), and both decorators call `_resolve_config(...)` first and then key on it -- `pld_cache` uses `(config, self._pld_cache_key(), None)` (lines ~178-186) and `horizon_pld_cache` uses `(config, self._pld_cache_key(n_steps=n_steps), n_steps)` (lines ~231-243). DiscretizationConfig is `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` (discretization.py:17-18), so it hashes and compares by value and two differently-valued globals cannot alias onto one entry. The comment's parenthetical convention is also already violated: packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_b_min_sep.py:228-234 calls `acc.set_discretization(mc_resolution=5e-2, mc_failure_probability=1e-2, seed=3)`, which is not `_MC_KW`. No open tracked issue covers this. Severity low and non-epsilon: it is a stale explanatory comment in a test; the test itself still asserts the right thing and passes.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A maintainer debugging PLD caching reads the comment at test_per_step.py:414-418, believes the cache is not keyed by the resolved DiscretizationConfig, and either sprinkles defensive `cache_clear()` calls (evicting shared entries that other tests' identity assertions rely on) or 'preserves' the stated cross-file `_MC_KW` convention when tightening the key -- a constraint that test_b_min_sep.py already breaks and that the value-keyed cache made unnecessary at 493a9f4a/819ef0d9.

verdicts.title: BallsInBins+IdentityMf composition case has zero PR-gate coverage: the fast test skips it and its replacement is marked slow
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced by execution, not just by reading. test_per_step_invariants.py:499-502 has the unmarked parametrized `test_supports_composition` skipping `('BallsInBins','IdentityMf')` with reason 'covered by the slow identity-composition case'; lines 511-517 define the stand-in `test_balls_in_bins_identity_supports_composition` under `@pytest.mark.slow`. .github/workflows/pr.yml pytest-marker values at lines 70, 93, 106, 118, 129 all include `and not slow`. Running `uv run pytest .../test_per_step_invariants.py::TestKPrefixInvariants -m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed' -k composition -rs` gives '7 passed, 1 skipped' with the skip reason printed, and `--collect-only` under the same marker does not list the module-level slow test. So on a PR the pair is skipped in one place and deselected in the other. I also grepped for an alternative: packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_identity_mf.py exercises `balls_in_bins(IdentityMf(...))` epsilon but never the `per_step(...) * K1 | ... * K2` composition path, so the gap is real. Not a duplicate of #695/#698 -- those are about tightening partial-epoch BallsInBins prefix bounds, a numerical-conservativeness question, not test-lane selection. Severity low: main still covers it, no epsilon impact, blast radius is 'found one merge late'.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A change to the BallsInBins K-prefix path breaks per-step composition for the IdentityMf inner. Under the PR marker expression the parametrized case self-skips ('covered by the slow identity-composition case') and the slow stand-in is deselected, so every PR lane reports green; the failure surfaces only on the post-merge main run, after the change has landed. No other test in packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests exercises that composition.

verdicts.title: Quickstart and the DP-SGD tutorial publish a Poisson-amplified epsilon for a torch.randperm shuffled fixed-batch loop
verdicts.reasoning: The structural claim reproduces exactly; the quantitative claim does not, and I corrected it down. Confirmed: docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:44-51 calibrates against `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(nm), sample_rate) * num_steps` and lines 79-91 then train with `torch.randperm` + contiguous slicing and print the Poisson epsilon; dp_sgd_training.ipynb cells 9 and 13 do the same and ship a committed output 'Final privacy: (epsilon=3.00, delta=1e-05)', with mkdocs.yml:59-61 setting `execute: false` so that literal number is published. Neither file contains PoissonSampler or DataLoader (grepped both). Poisson amplification genuinely does not apply to a shuffled equal-size partition, so the published figure has no applicable theorem behind it -- and closed issue #356's acceptance criterion ('every documented loop uses the sampler through a DataLoader and executes exactly the calibrated horizon') is unmet, so this is not tracked work. REFUTED, however, is the magnitude: the reporter's 'most generous honest accounting' ignores allocation-style amplification, which Opaque itself ships. Measured with the repo venv at the reporter's own calibrated nm=1.35682832673192: `random_allocation(gaussian(nm), num_bins=32, n_steps=32)` composed over 20 epochs = 2.830 (num_bins=31 variant: 2.880), versus the published 3.000 -- i.e. the closest applicable model gives a number BELOW what the docs print, not 6.3x above. Quickstart likewise: nm=1.105301145464182, RA(32 bins) x 10 epochs = 2.703 vs printed 3.046. So the claimed 18.85 / 245.76 / 199.10 'honest bounds' are not honest bounds; they are what you get by discarding all amplification. The residual real defects are (i) the published epsilon rests on the wrong subsampling theorem, and (ii) a genuine step-count under-count -- both loops execute one extra partial batch per epoch (32 releases against 31 accounted), so the tutorial makes 640 releases while accounting 620 (poisson*640 = 3.051 vs 3.000) and the quickstart executes 320 while calibrating 310. Note also that Opaque's random_allocation models independent balls-and-bins assignment (Feldman & Shenfeld 2026; Chua et al. 2025) while randperm gives an exactly-equal-size shuffle partition, so strictly neither shipped accountant is a proven bound for the deployed loop -- which is the point, but the gap is a few percent, not a factor of six. Severity demoted high -> medium accordingly: an unsupported-theorem claim in flagship onboarding docs, not a user shipping a wildly wrong epsilon.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user follows the Quick Start or dp_sgd_training.ipynb and reports epsilon=3.00 for their model. The loop draws batches by `torch.randperm` + contiguous slicing -- a shuffled equal-size partition -- while the number was calibrated and reported under `dpsgd_acc.poisson(...)`, whose subsampling theorem does not apply to that sampler, and neither doc constructs a sampler at all. The published figure is therefore not backed by an applicable amplification result. Separately and independently, both loops execute one more optimizer step per epoch than they account for (32 batches vs `n_samples // batch_size` = 31), so the tutorial charges 620 releases for 640 executed (3.000 charged vs 3.051) and the quickstart charges 310 for 320 (3.046 printed against a 3.0 budget). The magnitude of the theorem mismatch is small, not large: recomputing at the same noise multiplier under Opaque's own `random_allocation` accountant -- the closest shipped model for shuffled fixed-size batching -- gives 2.830 for the tutorial and 2.703 for the quickstart, i.e. at or below the published numbers.

verdicts.title: Trainer docs advertise mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' while the runtime builds a plain PoissonSampler against the cyclic-group CyclicPoisson accountant
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link, including by execution. (1) docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:142 lists '| mf_band | b_min_sep (or explicit poisson) | {"bands": 16} |' with no caveat. (2) _training_arguments.py:181-193 allow-lists `mf_band -> {b_min_sep, poisson}` with the in-code comment calling poisson 'a looser-but-valid alternative'. (3) _dpftrl.py:224-232 `build_sampler` for sampling_mode='poisson' returns `PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=..., n_steps=..., ...)` from opaque.dpsgd.sampling -- no bands, no separation, independent draws every step. (4) _dpftrl.py:138-152 `build_amplifier_factory` for the same mode returns `_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, strategy), ...)` = CyclicPoisson, whose `pld_at` (_poisson.py:178-215) composes only `num_groups = ceil(rounded / bands)` per-group Poisson-Gaussian PLDs at `effective_nm = nm / sensitivity`. (5) `BandMfStrategy.sensitivity` is participation-blind -- I measured 0.9999999999999999 for (min_sep=1, max_participations=1000), (10, 100) and (1, 1) alike -- so nothing rescales the noise to pay for lost separation. (6) CyclicPoisson.min_sep is hardcoded to 1 with a comment admitting 'Cyclic Poisson provides no worst-case separation guarantee'. The b-group factorization in Choquette-Choo et al. (2023) is licensed by b-min-separated (cyclic) participation, under which a record's columns in the b-banded C have disjoint support so the run factors into ceil(n/b) independent one-participation Gaussians; plain Poisson gives min_sep=1, allows up to b participations inside one band block with overlapping columns, and the factorization is simply unsound -- the code charges one subsampled participation per b steps at sensitivity 1. Empirically the undercharge shows up as `poisson(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=10)), sample_rate=0.01, n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.7180` versus 1.8282 for the identity strategy under the identical deployed sampler -- the full factor-b composition saving is claimed without the separation that earns it. The in-code 'looser-but-valid' comment is wrong in the unsafe direction. Worst of all, the matching sampler exists and is wired: _dpftrl.py:282-294 has a working `cyclic_poisson` branch building `CyclicPoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate, bands=mf.strategy.bands, ...)`, and band-mf.md:295 tells users to 'Pair with CyclicPoissonSampler' -- but I confirmed by running TrainingArguments that mf_band + 'cyclic_poisson' is rejected ('allowed: [b_min_sep, poisson]') while mf_band + 'poisson' is accepted. So the allow-list admits precisely the wrong one of the two. Not a duplicate: open #359 concerns BandMfStrategy.sensitivity() semantics and paired second moments inside opaque-accounting/opaque-dpftrl; this is a trainer wiring + docs defect in opaque-transformers with its own one-line fix (swap 'poisson' for 'cyclic_poisson' in the mf_band allow-list, or reject it), and it is not among #319's sub-issues (347/353/355/359/360/361/362). Severity high, epsilon-affecting, unsafe direction.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user sets TrainingArguments(privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band', sampling_mode='poisson') -- presented at training-arguments.md:142 as a supported alternative with no warning, and accepted by the allow-list. build_sampler hands training a plain opaque.dpsgd.sampling.PoissonSampler over the whole dataset (independent per-step draws, min_sep=1, a record can appear in consecutive steps), while build_amplifier_factory prices the run through CyclicPoisson, which composes only ceil(n_steps/bands) per-group Poisson-Gaussian PLDs at effective_nm = nm/1.0. The ceil(n/b) group factorization is licensed only by b-min-separated participation; the deployed sampler provides none, and BandMfStrategy.sensitivity returns 1.0 regardless of min_sep or max_participations, so nothing compensates. The reported epsilon is materially undercharged -- at nm=1.0, q=0.01, n_steps=1000, bands=10 it reads 0.7180 while the same sampler under independent (identity) noise already costs 1.8282. Meanwhile CyclicPoissonSampler, the sampler that actually matches this accountant and that band-mf.md:295 instructs users to pair with, is built by build_sampler but rejected by the mf_band allow-list.

verdicts.title: Two mechanism pages and the DP-SGD guide instruct accounting the bounded Gaussian with the unbounded accountant; a third page says the accountant does not cover it
verdicts.reasoning: Every cited line and every measurement reproduces. Docs contradiction is real: gaussian.md:176-177 says 'Treat bound= as experimental: dpsgd_acc.gaussian() does not cover this variant', then gaussian.md:195-198 hands the reader `# Accounting (unchanged from the unbounded mechanism)` with `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), ...)`; dp-sgd.md:95-99 says 'pass bound=... -- same accounting' with no hedge at all; noise.md:177 carries the correct warning while noise.md:146-148 claims 'No probability mass sits at the boundaries'. Implementation checked directly: _gaussian.py:277-285 computes alpha/beta from erf, remaps u into [alpha,beta], inverts, then applies `torch.clamp(sample, min=low, max=high)`. Measured over a 200k-element ClippedPytree(max_norm=1.0) with gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.0, bound=B, key=key(0)): center 0.0/bound 1.0 -> realized sd 0.5409 (reported noise_stddev 1.0); center 5.0/bound 1.0 -> 0.040% of mass exactly at +B, 1060 distinct values, sd 0.2137; center 50.0/bound 1.0 and center 10.0/bound 3.0 -> 100% of mass at the boundary, sd exactly 0.0, one distinct value, i.e. a deterministic zero-noise release at the documented bound=3.0. So noise.md's 'no mass at the boundaries' is false and noise_stddev reports the nominal, not realized, scale. The path is trainer-reachable: _dp_trainer.py:1544-1562 filters privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs to ('bound','compute_dtype') and functools.partials them into gaussian_noise while the accountant stays the plain Gaussian -- and truncation strictly REDUCES realized noise below what is charged, the unsafe direction. However: issue #344 'Deploy a Gaussian mechanism that matches the accountant' (in the open-issues snapshot; GitHub now shows it closed as not_planned on 2026-08-27) states verbatim that 'The bounded mode ... can collapse outside the interval, and reports a nominal variance that downstream bias correction assumes is realized' while 'accounting prices an unbounded Gaussian', with acceptance criteria 'Extreme centers cannot produce deterministic zero-noise releases' and 'Reported noise metadata matches downstream semantics'. Evidence items (a) and (b) of this finding are that issue restated, so I am marking it tracked under 344 rather than new. The one genuinely untracked slice is the documentation itself -- #344 says nothing about docs -- so gaussian.md:195 and dp-sgd.md:96 will keep instructing an unsound accounting even if #344 stays not_planned; that is a cheap standalone docs fix and should not be lost in the dedup. Severity demoted high -> medium: the mechanism-level privacy defect is #344's, the variant is labelled experimental on two of the four pages, and what remains new here is a documentation contradiction.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user enables gaussian_noise(..., bound=3.0) -- reachable from DPTrainer via privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs, which _dp_trainer.py:1544-1562 forwards verbatim -- and calibrates and reports epsilon with `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(nm), q) * steps`, exactly as gaussian.md:195-198 shows and dp-sgd.md:96 states without qualification. The deployed mechanism is a per-coordinate truncated-and-clamped Gaussian, not the unbounded one the PLD prices, and truncation removes noise rather than adding it: measured at nm=1.0 the realized sd is 0.5409 at bound=1.0 and 0.3400 at bound=3.0/center 5.0, while noise_stddev keeps reporting 1.0 to the optimizer bias correction. When a clipped gradient sum sits well outside the interval -- routine at max_norm=1.0 without normalize_by -- the release collapses to a constant at the boundary (center 10.0, bound 3.0: sd 0.0, one distinct value, 100% of mass at +B), directly contradicting noise.md:146-148's 'No probability mass sits at the boundaries'. Two pages (gaussian.md:176-177, noise.md:177) already warn that dpsgd_acc.gaussian() does not cover this variant, so the docs contradict themselves within the same file.
